lesson.menu_title: Making Connections at a Conference -- A Welcome Reception in Houston
lesson.menu_desc: A chemical industry conference in Houston: meet a mutual contact at the welcome reception, give your elevator pitch, and add extra information about people, companies, and places with who / which / where / whose and commas ('Greg, who works in New York, put me in touch with you') -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 29 -- Making Connections at a Conference
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Lucimara | Lesson 29 -- Making Connections at a Conference
lesson.grammar_point: non-defining relative clauses (who / which / where / whose, with commas)

listenings.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to ChemConnect Americas here in Houston. My name is Paul Walker, and I'm the event director. A few quick notes before the reception starts. Please wear your name badge at all times, because security will ask for it at every door. Tomorrow's keynote, which starts at nine a.m. in the Grand Ballroom, will be given by Doctor Karen Lee, whose research on green chemistry won an award last year. After lunch, there are four breakout sessions, and you can choose one on the conference app. The panel on supply chains, which many of you asked about, has moved to Room B, where there are more seats. Finally, if you want to meet new people, the lounge on the second floor is open until ten. Enjoy the evening.

When I go to a conference, I always prepare my elevator pitch, which is just thirty seconds long. I say my name, where I'm based, and one thing that makes my company different. Then I stop talking and I ask a question. Last year in Chicago, I met a buyer, whose company was looking for a new supplier. I didn't sell anything that night. I just listened. Two days later, I reached out by email, and I mentioned something he told me about his daughter, who was starting college. He answered in ten minutes. My advice is simple: talk less, remember more, and always follow up within forty-eight hours. People forget faces, but they remember how you made them feel.

extra_audio.text: First, I find a person with an interesting name badge and say hello. Then, I give my elevator pitch: my name, where I'm based, and what my company does. Next, I mention our mutual contact, who put us in touch. After that, I suggest a meeting at a breakout session, where we can talk business. Finally, I reach out by email within forty-eight hours.
